heard: One sleeping black hole flared 50 times brighter than the Crab Nebula. Located about 8,000 light years away, V404 Cygni holds a black hole 9 to 10 times our sun's mass. Every 6.5 days, a companion star orbits closely, feeding gas into a swelling accretion disk. After recorded outbursts in 1938 and 1956, Japan's Jenga satellite detected another awakening in 1989. Then, after 26 years of slumber, NASA's Swift satellite caught it erupting in June 2015. Extreme gravitational frame-dragging warped spacetime, forcing its inner disk to wobble like a dying top. Terrifyingly, relativistic plasma jet-sprayed high-energy bullets in wildly changing directions within minutes. Decades of silence can shatter in seconds whenever this cosmic predator awakens.
